rows.description: A child forgets bottles, loses worksheets and works in bursts when interest strikes. Feels bad about reminders and is not lazy; simple routines and visual checklists help more than scolding.

rows.description: A teenager makes timetables, colour-codes notes and feels guilty on any unplanned day. Discipline is a real strength, but rigid plans can turn into self-punishment when life interrupts.

rows.description: A wise teenager keeps a plan but builds slack into it, treating a missed day as information rather than failure. Consistency counts more than perfection, and sleep is part of the plan.

rows.description: A young adult prefers to decide late, keep options open and adapt as things unfold. Works well in changing situations, yet deadlines and shared commitments need deliberate anchors.

rows.description: A team notices the person who always delivers on time, remembers details and quietly fixes gaps. They are trusted, but may be over-relied on and unthanked until they burn out.

rows.description: A toddler waves at strangers, seeks people to play beside and gets loud with excitement. Energy rises around others and dips when alone; adults still teach gentle limits.

rows.description: A child makes friends easily, leads games and feels restless during silent seat work. Gains energy from company, and can miss quiet cues from friends who need space.
